reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 and E2 describe sputtering of different materials (NbMoTaW films, ITO) and do not mention TiN coatings, oxidation resistance, or the HfNbTaTiZr alloy. E3 discusses phase stability in HfNbTaTiZr but not coatings. E4 describes compression testing of an unspecified material, not coated HfNbTaTiZr. No evidence supports the barrier, adhesion, or mechanical property retention claims.
premises: TiN coatings can be applied to refractory alloys via magnetron sputtering
TiN acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier at 1000°C in air
A TiN coating will adhere to and protect HfNbTaTiZr
The coating will not degrade the alloy's high-temperature strength
The coating will not degrade the alloy's room-temperature ductility
